title: Pages — the shell, round 4: the page view's own frame and side panel

steps.path: Any open page, the band across the top
steps.headline: The page view gets its own top band: panel toggle left, page name centre, Back to chat right, window buttons kept.
steps.changed: Built from your round-3 description. Where the app's band has Settings and Projects, this one has the panel toggle; where the session strip sits, the page's icon and name; where Session Files and Games sit, Esc · Back to chat; the minimise, maximise and close buttons stay put.
steps.notice: Esc still leaves the page. Nothing from the chat band (session strip, files, games) is on this band.
steps.risk: Edit in chat sits beside the page name; you did not place it, so the question at the end asks where it belongs.

steps.path: The panel on the left of an open page
steps.headline: The side panel lists every page, grouped like the library, with its pin beside each; Manage pages is centred at the bottom.
steps.changed: All pages, not only pinned ones: Personal first, then each project. The current page is marked. The pin beside a page pins or unpins it without opening it. Manage pages opens the full Pages screen.
steps.notice: You can hop between pages without leaving the page view. Pins here and in the library are the same pins.
steps.risk: A long list of pages scrolls inside the panel; there is no search in it yet.

steps.path: The toggle at the top-left of the page view
steps.headline: The panel collapses with the button at the top-left, and the page takes the full width.
steps.changed: One click hides the panel; the same button brings it back. The page's rounded pane grows to fill the space.
steps.notice: A page you are working in can have the whole window.
steps.risk: Whether the panel stays collapsed the next time you open a page is not decided; the shell forgets it for now.

steps.path: Click another page in the panel
steps.headline: Clicking a page in the panel opens it in place; here the planner gave way to the paint studio.
steps.changed: The panel row is the switch. The band's name and icon follow the page.
steps.notice: Switching pages is one click, like switching sessions in the strip.
steps.risk: Switching away and back reloads the page, so a page's unsaved working state is lost on a switch until pages get their own memory.

steps.path: Wherever Edit in chat ends up
steps.headline: Where should Edit in chat live now that the page's edge is quiet?
steps.today: Edit in chat is a small ghost button beside the page's name in the top band. You did not ask for it there; it needed a home after the Pin and Edit chips went.
steps.problem: It is the way a page gets changed, so it has to be findable, but the top band is meant to stay quiet.

options.label: Beside the name
pros: Always in view while the page is open
cons: A button in the band you wanted quiet

options.label: In the side panel
pros: Keeps the band to name and navigation only
cons: Hidden when the panel is collapsed

options.label: Only in the library
pros: Nothing extra on the page view at all
cons: Editing means leaving the page first
